data.projectSynopsis: This is a React-based TodoMVC application that implements a classic todo list manager. The app uses React 17.0.2 with a reducer-based state management pattern (useReducer hook) to manage todo items. It features routing via react-router-dom with routes for 'All', 'Active', and 'Completed' views. The UI includes a header, main content area with todo items, and a footer with a 'Clear completed' button. The application is built with webpack and served via a local development server. It follows the MVC pattern where the Model is a Todo reducer, the View consists of React UI components, and the Controller is the App component with useReducer hook.

readme.excerpt: # TodoMVC: React ## Description This application uses React 17.0.2 to implement a todo application. - [React](https://reactjs.org/) is a JavaScript library for creating user interfaces. ## Implementation details React focuses mainly on providing composable user interfaces to enable developers to build an appealing website or web app. React does not force the user to utilize a particular design pattern, but it does provide useful hooks to implement an MVC pattern, if desired. React:\ Model: Todo reducer (reducer.js)\ View: React ui components\ Controller: App component + useReducer hook MVC:\ Model: Maintains the data and behavior of an application\ View: Displays the model in the ui\ Controller: Serves as an interface between view & model components ## Build steps To build the static files, this application utilizes webpack. It minifies and optimizes output files and copies all necessary files to a `dist` folder. ## Requirements The only requirement is an installation of Node, to be able to install dependencies and run scripts to serve a local server. ``` * Node (min version: 18.13.0) * NPM (min version: 8.19.3) ``` ## Local preview ``` terminal: 1. npm install 2. npm run serve ```

steps.rationale: The app is a TodoMVC todo list. I have already added a todo and clicked the 'All' filter. The 'Completed' filter link is available and unexplored. Clicking it will show only completed todos, which is a useful ordinary interaction to understand the filtering behavior. This broadens coverage across the filter controls.
steps.expectedOutcome: The view filters to show only completed todos; since none are completed, the list likely becomes empty and the count updates accordingly.

steps.rationale: The interface shows a todo list with filter tabs (All, Active, Completed) and an input for new todos. I've already filled and submitted a todo. The safe action is to click the 'Active' link, which is a visible navigation/filter control. This helps understand the filtering behavior across todo states.
steps.expectedOutcome: Clicking 'Active' should filter to show only active (incomplete) todos, updating the visible list and the count indicator accordingly.
